chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from al-Harithi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man in whom there is stinginess, envy, and cowardice does not have faith. The believer is not cowardly, nor stingy, nor acquisitive.
ai.seo_question: What are the key character traits that prevent a person from having true faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three specific vices—stinginess, envy, and cowardice, and greed—as fundamental defects that invalidate the integrity of faith, reflecting the Shia emphasis on moral perfection (kamal) as an intrinsic marker of iman. This triad is often contrasted with the virtues of generosity, courage, and contentment, illustrating how inner character directly manifests in spiritual reality. The hadith serves as a diagnostic tool for believers to assess the authenticity of their faith through self-examination of these core traits.

en.badr-shahin: My father, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to us from Sa’d bin Abdullah from … al-Harithi that Abu Abdullah (a) said:
Anyone who enjoys stinginess, envy, and cowardice cannot be believer. The believer is never coward, stingy, or acquisitive.
